metadata.structure: SAH English Grades 5-10 September 2026, semester one
metadata.note: Grades 5–6 vocabulary, reading, writing and grammar reviewed by taught units; space unit now correct. Existing listening audio requires regeneration from the revised unit scripts; mixed paper D carries intact source sections.

activities.title: Listening 1 · Match dialogues to pictures
passages: At the talent show I will play the drum with my classmates. We have practised the rhythm every afternoon, and the music teacher will help us on stage.
My older sister will play the piano in front of the audience. She has learned a new song and practises it after school.
My uncle is bringing a camera to take photographs of the performers. He will ask permission before sharing the pictures.
Salma will read a poem from her own book while the other students listen quietly. She wrote the poem last weekend.
Huda will use a paintbrush to make a picture as the orchestra plays. She chose bright colours for the final performance.

activities.title: Listening 2 · Dialogue / interview
activities.passage: Interviewer: Welcome to School Stage. When will the talent show start, Salma? Salma: On Thursday afternoon. Interviewer: Where will students perform? Salma: In the school hall. Interviewer: What will you do? Salma: Play the piano with my brother. Interviewer: Who will introduce the groups? Salma: Our English teacher, Ms Aisha. Interviewer: What should families do? Salma: Arrive ten minutes early and stay quiet during performances.

questions.stem: Rana is ____ than her sister at telling stories.
Of all the performers, Hamed was the ____.
Maha is good at ____ a football.
The youngest singer was ____ than the older girls.
Salim is the ____ student in our drama team.

activities.title: Reading 2 · True or False
activities.passage: Last Thursday, our school held a talent show in the hall. Huda played a lively tune on her drum while her friends sang. After the music, Salma read a poem that she had written about her grandmother. She was nervous at first, but the audience listened carefully. Later, Nasser played the piano, and Mariam painted a picture beside the stage. A teacher took photographs for the school website, but she asked the performers for permission first. The show began at three o'clock and finished at five. The students put away the instruments and cleaned the hall before going home.

activities.title: Listening 1 · Match dialogues to pictures
passages: My grandfather crossed the bay in a small wooden boat when he was young. Now we travel along the new road instead.
My grandmother rode a bicycle to school every morning. Today, many children take the school bus.
The old classroom had a large clock above the board. There were no computers in the room.
My father walked to school when he was little, but I take a bus because our home is much farther away.
My mother took family photographs using a camera with film. Today we can see pictures immediately on our phones.

activities.title: Listening 2 · Dialogue / interview

Interviewer: How many classrooms were there? Hamad: Three. Interviewer: What did children play after school? Hamad: Football in an open field. Interviewer: What does he like about schools today? Hamad: The library and computers.

activities.title: Reading 2 · True or False
activities.passage: My grandfather showed me some photographs of his childhood last weekend. His school was small and had only three classrooms. The children walked there because their families did not own cars. He used a pencil and paper to write his lessons. There were no computers or digital boards. After school, he played football in an empty field. His family had an old camera, but they waited several days before the pictures were printed. Today I travel to a larger school by bus. I use a computer during science lessons and can take pictures with a phone. My grandfather says that many things have changed, but good friends and hard work are important in every generation.

questions.stem: He travelled to school by car.

activities.title: Listening 1 · Match dialogues to pictures
passages: A: What is the science team building for the fair? B: We are making a rocket model from recycled paper. We will show how a real rocket travels into space. A: Will it actually fly? B: No, it is just a model for our display.

A: How will we look at stars on Friday evening? B: We will use a telescope. It makes distant objects in the sky easier to see. A: Can I look directly at the Sun through it? B: Never! That is dangerous.

A: What are those eight round objects on your poster? B: They represent the planets in our solar system. Earth is one of them, and they all move around the Sun. A: Shall we add their names? B: Yes, below the pictures.
A: Why is the astronaut wearing special clothes? B: It is a spacesuit. It protects the astronaut outside a spacecraft. A: Could we wear ordinary jackets in space? B: No, they would not protect us.
A: What is the bright shape in the night sky? B: It is the Moon, Earth's natural satellite. A: Does it make its own light? B: No, it reflects sunlight.

activities.title: Listening 2 · Dialogue / interview
activities.passage: Interviewer: Welcome to Young Space Explorers. What will your class make for the science fair, Mariam? Mariam: A large model of the solar system. Interviewer: How many planets will you put around the Sun? Mariam: Eight planets. Interviewer: Which planet do we live on? Mariam: Earth. Interviewer: What will you use to look at the Moon? Mariam: A telescope on the school roof. Interviewer: What will you do before the exhibition? Mariam: We will check that every planet has the correct name. Interviewer: When will the exhibition open? Mariam: On Thursday morning.

We ____ travel to the Moon tomorrow. It is only a class project.
____ far is the Moon from Earth?
Our guide ____ show us the telescope next week.
____ large is the new space station?

activities.title: Reading 2 · True or False
activities.passage: Dear Space Explorers, Today I am writing about our visit to the science centre. At first we saw a large model of the solar system. The guide explained that eight planets move around the Sun and that Earth is one of them. We watched a short video about astronauts living on a space station. They wear spacesuits when they work outside. Later we looked at a telescope, but the guide reminded us never to look directly at the Sun through it. I enjoyed learning about the Moon, which travels around Earth. Next week our class will make a model rocket and write a short blog about the exhibition. I hope we can visit the centre again.

activities.title: Listening 1 · Match dialogues to pictures
passages: I am buying a fresh apple from the fruit stall. The oranges are nice, but I only have enough money for one piece of fruit.
I saved three rials to buy my cousin a birthday gift. I will compare prices before choosing something useful.
I found a book about sea animals at the bookshop. It costs two rials, and I have saved exactly that amount.
The larger cup was too expensive, so I chose this blue cup for my grandmother. I brought my own shopping bag.
My father and I visit the local market on Friday mornings. We buy vegetables from several different stalls.

activities.title: Listening 2 · Dialogue / interview
activities.passage: Interviewer: Who are you shopping for today, Ahmed? Ahmed: My sister. It is her birthday. Interviewer: How much money did you save? Ahmed: Five rials. Interviewer: Where will you go first? Ahmed: To the bookshop, because she loves stories. Interviewer: How much is the adventure book? Ahmed: Three rials. Interviewer: Will you buy a plastic bag? Ahmed: No, I have a cloth bag. Interviewer: What about the remaining money? Ahmed: I will save the two rials.

activities.title: Reading 2 · True or False
activities.passage: Last Saturday, my friend Ahmed and I went shopping for his sister's birthday. Ahmed had saved five rials in his money box. We looked at the toys first, but the prices were too high. Then we visited the bookshop, where a friendly assistant showed us some adventure stories. Ahmed chose a colourful book that cost three rials. He kept the receipt and put the book in his cloth bag. We walked past the bakery and looked at the cakes, but we did not buy anything else. Ahmed decided to save the remaining two rials. His sister was delighted with the book, and Ahmed was happy that he had stayed within his budget.

questions.stem: They bought a toy from the first shop.

activities.title: Listening 1 · Match dialogues to pictures
passages: After finishing my homework I play football with my neighbours at the small field. We meet there three evenings a week.
I joined the school music club to learn the drum. We practise rhythms every Monday with our teacher.
I love riding my bicycle on quiet paths. My father checks my helmet before we leave the house.
The wind is strong today, so we will fly our kite in the open park away from roads and power lines.
During the holiday I started painting. My aunt lent me a paintbrush and I made a picture of our garden.

activities.title: Listening 2 · Dialogue / interview
activities.passage: Interviewer: When does the free-time club meet, Yousuf? Yousuf: Every Saturday. Interviewer: Where do members meet? Yousuf: At the community sports centre. Interviewer: Which activity was popular last month? Yousuf: Cycling. Interviewer: Do children bring their own bicycles? Yousuf: No, the centre lends bicycles and helmets. Interviewer: What will you try next Saturday? Yousuf: Table tennis indoors.

questions.stem: Listen! My friends ____ music in the garden.

passages.stem: Every Saturday, Amina joins a sports club at the community centre. She enjoys football and cycling. The coaches remind children to warm up and drink water before activities. New members can borrow helmets and bicycles from the club.
Salim loves music. He joined a drumming group at school and practises with friends every Monday. At home, he listens to new rhythms and tries to copy them. His parents enjoy hearing his progress.

Maha likes quiet hobbies. She paints pictures of birds and flowers, then sends photographs to her cousin. She sometimes visits the park to find new ideas. She uses a small paintbrush and keeps her colours in a box.

questions.stem: Which text describes football and cycling?
Which text mentions borrowing safety equipment?
Which text mentions sharing pictures with a cousin?
Which text mentions looking for ideas in a park?

activities.title: Reading 2 · True or False
activities.passage:
From: amina@school.example
To: reem@school.example
Subject: Our new free-time club
Dear Reem,
Last Saturday I joined the free-time club at the community sports centre. We met at nine in the morning. First, our coach showed us how to check bicycle helmets. Then we tried a short cycling course. I was nervous at the beginning, but a friend helped me. We also played a team game before lunch. Next Saturday we will try table tennis inside the centre. The club lends its equipment, so nobody needs to buy an expensive bicycle. I hope you can join us next week. Please ask the sports teacher by Thursday if you want to come.
Best wishes,
Amina

questions.stem: The club met on Saturday morning.
Amina bought an expensive new bicycle.
Her friend helped her during the cycling activity.
The club will try table tennis next Saturday.
Reem must contact a bus driver.

passages: I am using a computer to design our class poster. It is easier to correct the headings on the screen.
Our science team built a small robot that follows a black line. It moves because of the program we wrote.
We will use a camera to record the experiment. We can compare the results before and after adding water.
The classroom has a digital clock that shows the lesson time clearly. We use it during short group challenges.
I borrowed a book about inventions from the library. It explains how technology changed life in the past.

activities.title: Listening 2 · Dialogue / interview
activities.passage: Interviewer: What did you build for the technology exhibition, Fatma? Fatma: A robot that waters plants. Interviewer: How does it check dry soil? Fatma: With a sensor connected to a computer program. Interviewer: Who helped you with the wires? Fatma: My older sister. Interviewer: Where did you demonstrate it? Fatma: At our school science exhibition. Interviewer: What will you add next? Fatma: A warning light for an empty water tank.

questions.stem: How does it check the soil?
Where did she show the robot?
My grandfather ____ use a tablet when he was young.
This new laptop works ____ than our old one.
I ____ send the message because the internet was down.
The students ____ save their files before leaving yesterday.

passages.stem: Our science club designed a robot to water plants when the soil became dry. The students connected a sensor to a simple program. They tested the model several times before showing it at the school exhibition.

The digital photography group used a camera to record an experiment. The students took pictures before and after adding water. They compared the results on a computer and explained their findings to the class.

Mariam wrote an online safety guide for younger pupils. She advised students not to share passwords and to ask an adult before downloading unknown files. Her teacher checked the guide before it appeared on the class website.

questions.stem: Which text describes a robot that waters plants?
Which text uses photographs to compare results?
Which text explains using a computer to study an experiment?
Which text gives advice about passwords?

activities.title: Reading 2 · True or False
activities.passage:
From: fatma@school.example
To: salma@school.example
Subject: Our technology project
Dear Salma,
Yesterday we presented our new robot at the school science exhibition. It can water a small plant when a sensor detects dry soil. My sister helped me check the wires safely, and I wrote a simple program on the computer. At first the sensor gave the wrong reading. We moved it and tested the robot again. The model worked during the exhibition, and our teacher was pleased. Next month we hope to add a light to show when the water tank is empty. Please visit our technology club on Tuesday if you would like to see it.
Best wishes,
Fatma

questions.stem: The sensor worked perfectly from the beginning.
They tested the robot again after changing the sensor position.
They hope to add a warning light.

activities.title: Writing 2 · Short review
activities.prompt: Write a review of a school technology demonstration. Explain what the invention does, why it is useful, and how it could improve. Write at least 50 words.

passages: I need a book about Omani history, so I am visiting the public library near the roundabout. It closes at six.
The old wooden boats are displayed inside the museum beside the fort. A guide tells visitors about sea trade.
My brother hurt his ankle, so we will visit the clinic opposite the supermarket this afternoon.
We buy vegetables and fresh fish at the market behind the bus station. It is busiest in the morning.
Our family walked along the beach at the weekend. We collected litter, but did not swim because the waves were strong.

activities.title: Listening 2 · Dialogue / interview
activities.passage: Interviewer: What is your favourite place in town, Dana? Dana: The public library. Interviewer: Where can we find it? Dana: Opposite the main park, beside the post office. Interviewer: When does it open on weekdays? Dana: At nine in the morning. Interviewer: What can children do there? Dana: Read and join story club. Interviewer: What happens every Wednesday? Dana: A librarian runs a reading activity. Interviewer: How do you get there? Dana: I walk with my father.

questions.stem: We ____ towards the museum when it started to rain.
This is the building ____ my uncle works.
A guide is a person ____ helps visitors.
At four o’clock, the tourists ____ photos near the bridge.
I met a woman ____ lives beside the old fort.

passages.stem: The public library is opposite the main park, beside the post office. It opens at nine on weekdays and has a quiet study room. Children can borrow books and join a story club every Wednesday.
The town museum displays old boats and photographs of the harbour. Visitors can learn about journeys along the coast. Our class listened to a guide explain how people traded goods in the past.
The community clinic is next to the market. A nurse helps families who need medical advice. The clinic opens in the morning and afternoon, but people should telephone before visiting on holidays.

questions.stem: Which text mentions a study room?
Which text describes old boats and a harbour?
Which text is about a health service?
Which text advises calling before visiting on holidays?

activities.title: Reading 2 · True or False
activities.passage:
From: dana@school.example
To: reem@school.example
Subject: A place I recommend
Dear Reem,
I visited our town library with my father last Wednesday. It is opposite the main park, next to the post office. We arrived at ten in the morning. A librarian showed us the children's reading area and helped me choose a book about Oman. At eleven, we joined a storytelling activity with other pupils. My father borrowed a history book, and we walked home before lunch. I want to visit the museum next weekend because it has photographs of old boats. If you are free on Wednesday, we can go to the library together.
Best wishes,
Dana

questions.stem: Dana visited the library on Wednesday.
The library is beside the airport.
A librarian helped Dana find a book.
Dana's father borrowed a history book.
Dana has already visited the museum this weekend.
